headline: Foster + Partners and Aedas confirmed for INDEX Saudi design talks
deck: The interiors show's talks programme runs on five pillars, one of which asks what Saudi architectural heritage contributes to contemporary specification.
excerpt: INDEX Saudi Arabia's Design Talks programme has confirmed speakers from Foster + Partners, Aedas, Red Sea Global and Dar Global across five thematic pillars including heritage and materiality.
content:
INDEX Saudi Arabia, the interiors exhibition co-located with the Hotel and Hospitality Expo at Riyadh's convention centre from 15 September, runs a talks programme organised on five pillars: transformation, heritage, materiality, intelligence and experience.

The confirmed speakers span international practices and Saudi institutions. Tarek Hassan, associate partner at Foster + Partners, and Daniel Abecasis, executive director at Aedas, represent the large international architectural firms working on Saudi projects. Yahya Alghamdi appears from Red Sea Global and Rahaf Abusamra from Dar Global, both developer-side. Fatemah Almadani, chief executive of Maamor Interior, and Jawaher Al Moarawi of Grid Design bring the Saudi practice perspective, and Dr Mohammed Alnaim, associate professor and cultural heritage consultant at the University of Hail, the academic one.

The heritage pillar is the one that distinguishes this programme from an interiors show anywhere else, and it reflects a genuine specification question rather than a cultural gesture. Saudi Arabia's development programme has committed publicly to architecture that reads as local rather than as internationally interchangeable, and the Royal Commission for Riyadh City and Diriyah have both built that requirement into design briefs. Translating it into interiors is harder than into facades. A Najdi exterior vocabulary is well documented and reasonably easy to reference; the interior equivalent — materials, proportions, joinery, the handling of light and privacy — is less codified, and specifying it at the volume a hotel programme requires means finding manufacturers who can produce it consistently.

That is where the materiality pillar connects to the exhibition floor. An architect can draw a detail; someone has to make it in quantities of several hundred rooms, to a brand standard, on a fixed delivery date. The gap between a heritage-referencing design intent and a supply chain able to deliver it is a real constraint on Saudi projects, and it is one of the reasons contract furniture and joinery suppliers have been establishing regional capability rather than shipping from Europe or the Far East.

The intelligence pillar covers the same ground the hospitality summit addresses from the operations side — building systems, guest-room technology and the data infrastructure behind them.

INDEX's supporting partners include Geberit as design talks sponsor, the Royal Institute of British Architects as architectural knowledge partner and the Chartered Institute of Building as association partner. The co-located LIGHTSPACE Saudi Arabia covers lighting, positioned by the organiser against a Saudi lighting market it states at $2.1bn.

Speaker names and programme pillars are taken from the organiser's published talks page. A note of caution for anyone consulting the shared exhibitor directory platform: it returns a roster of UAE entities that belongs to the Dubai edition of INDEX, not to the Riyadh show.
